snippet.title: Exploring Bangkok Walking the Beat
snippet.description:
Bangkok isn’t just a city you visit — it’s a city you experience. Walking the beat here means diving headfirst into vibrant street life, sacred temples, buzzing markets, and the rhythm of everyday Thai culture. Lace up your shoes — this is how to explore Bangkok on foot.

Start in the historic heart of the city:

Wat Phra Kaew – Thailand’s most sacred temple.

Grand Palace – Stunning architecture and former royal residence.

Wat Pho – Home of the famous Reclining Buddha and traditional Thai massage school.

Cross the river to Wat Arun – Especially magical at sunset.

💡 Tip: Dress modestly (covered shoulders & knees).

snippet.title: There's Been a Murder on My Thai Farm
snippet.description:
The mission! Post the Peep Show "tribute" video, then immediately execute the plan on Twitter. They have to see it! It's aimed squarely at their public-facing social media accounts. David Mitchell (@RealDMitchell) and Robert Webb (@arobertwebb).One of them will respond, eventually. It would be great if others could retweet and tag them too. I hope they don't sue me though! It's an homage, your honour!

Brand New Twitter: https://x.com/FarangFarmTH

I wonder how many people in Thailand have actually seen Peep Show? They're missing out if not, it's maybe the best British comedy of our generation!

But back to the topic at hand! There's been a murder on the farm. A triple homicide, to be precise. The victims? Three Siamese Rosewood trees. The prime suspects? A gang of cheerfully waddling ducks who seem to have a methodical passion for landscape demolition. A simple open-and-shut case.

...Except... oh, God. No. I saw it all coming, didn't I? The 'non-interventional observation'. That wasn't a great strategy. My own crippling analysis paralysis. The 20% rule, the botanical schism, Sophie's choice but with a tree... I don't mean to be overly dramatic, but, I'm definitely the Charles Manson of my own farm. The ducks were just my foolish followers.

Join me for a captivating look at our farm as we explore the growth of trees and the improvements in our landscape! 🌳 From innovative farming techniques to sustainable agriculture practices, this video showcases the journey of food production and plant breeding in action. Don't miss out on the insights into animal husbandry that make our farm thrive! 🐄✨

My slow descent to madness can be monitored on my website:

► https://farang-farm.com/

snippet.title: Who’s the Real Enemy in the Philippines?
snippet.description:
Who’s the real enemy in the Philippines?

After viral images and headlines showing the arrests of foreign YouTubers Vitaly Zdorovetskiy (VitalyzdTv) and Pro Life Traveler, many people treated it like a major victory.

This video is not a defense of law-breaking.
If you break local laws, consequences are expected.

What this video questions is priorities.

While attention is focused on two foreign vloggers, there’s a reality in the Philippines that doesn’t disappear when the cameras turn off:
• Poverty visible on the streets
• Families sleeping outside luxury areas
• Corruption complaints Filipinos openly talk about
• Drug problems acknowledged publicly
• And the gap between symbolic wins and real solutions

This is not influencer drama.
This is not clickbait.

It’s a truth-forward discussion built on lived observation and documented reality.

If a camera showing reality makes people uncomfortable, the solution isn’t to silence the camera — it’s to fix what’s being shown.

snippet.title: How Fertilizer KILLS The Soil Food Web
snippet.description:
Our crops are eating junk food… and so are we. Have you ever wondered why our food seems less flavorful and nutritious than it used to? This film is a journey to find the answer, starting in the vast rice fields of Thailand and leading deep into the heart of a living forest.

Thank you so much for joining me on this exploration into the world beneath our feet. For decades, modern industrial agriculture has relied on a simple but destructive formula: chemical fertilizers. We've been told that to grow anything, we need to constantly feed our soil with a cocktail of NPK (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium), but this approach has a hidden cost. We're trapped in a cycle of diminishing returns, using more and more chemicals just to get the same results, all while stripping our soil of its natural vitality and leaving our food nutrient-poor.

But what if there's a better way?

In this video, we contrast the chemical-dependent world of conventional farming with the thriving, self-sustaining ecosystem of a Thai forest. Here, we discover nature's incredible delivery system: the Soil Food Web. This is the bustling, microscopic city of fungi, bacteria, microbes, and insects that work in perfect harmony to break down organic matter and feed plants everything they need, in perfect balance. We'll explore the power of mycelium networks, the "superhighways of the soil," and see how this ancient system cycles more nutrients than an industrial farm, sustainably and for free.
This journey isn't just theoretical. We bring these lessons back to our own "Farang Farm" in Sisaket, Thailand to put the principles of regenerative farming to the test. Can we really bring dead, compacted clay soil back to life? Through hands-on experiments, we create our own fungal cultures and, with the help of a microscope, get a stunning up-close look at the beneficial hyphae that prove life is returning to our land.

This is a story about a paradigm shift, from fighting nature to working with it. It’s about rebuilding the living systems that can feed us and heal our planet. If you're interested in permaculture, sustainable living, soil health, or just want to see the incredible hidden world that supports all life, then this journey is for you.

To follow our progress and learn more about our projects here in Thailand, please visit our website:

Obtain a yield
Apply self-regulation & accept feedback

Produce no waste   
Design from patterns to details
Integrate rather than segregate
Use small and slow solutions   
Use and value diversity

snippet.title: Do You Need a Visa Agent in Thailand?
snippet.description:
1. When You DON’T Need a Visa Agent

For most travelers, doing it yourself is straightforward.

Examples:

Visa-free entry (many countries get up to ~60 days stay)

Tourist visa applications

Visa extensions at immigration offices

You simply:

Apply online or at a Thai embassy

Submit documents (passport, photos, hotel booking, flight)

Go to immigration for extensions if needed

Thousands of travelers handle this process themselves each year.

2. When a Visa Agent Can Be Helpful

Some situations are more complicated.

People often use agents for:

Retirement visas

Business / work visas

Long-term visas

Opening a Thai bank account

Complex paperwork

Agents handle paperwork, immigration visits, and document preparation, which saves time and stress.
